findings.title: Profile-weight sketch reintroduces the per-agent loop the slice forbids
findings.description:
The weight lookup is a Python comprehension over every active agent, run inside each `BulkForce.__call__`. Three things in the documents contradict it:
- **Defining constraint:** line 198 requires "No Python-level per-agent loops in any `BulkForce.__call__` implementation".
- **Slice plan entry:** it promises "O(1) Python overhead regardless of agent count".
- **The slice's own verification:** the grep at line 223 (`for.*eval_indices`) matches `for pi in state.profile_indices[eval_indices]`, so step 4 fails on the design's own sketch.

The lighter fix is a per-profile table indexed by profile: `np.array([p.cohesion_weight for p in profiles])[state.profile_indices[eval_indices]]`. That loop is over profiles, not agents, and it matches the architecture's "index-based dispatch" via lookup tables (100-arch, GPU compute path). The "precompute per tick if needed" deferral at line 136 can then be dropped.

findings.title: Zero-sum leadership guard is not carried into the vectorized design
findings.description:
"Handling Zero-Neighbor Agents" covers only `counts[i] == 0`, and only shows the `np.maximum(counts, 1)` guard for cohesion. `LeadershipForce` gets one line ("weighted mean with leadership array", line 248).

Slice 102 requires that an agent whose neighbors all have zero leadership receives zero force, guarded by an epsilon on the leadership sum. In a loop that is a `continue`; in a vectorized weighted mean it is a 0/0 that yields NaN for the whole row. This is the default state, not a corner case: 102 initializes `leadership` to zeros, so a naive rewrite puts NaN into every agent's force and then into positions.

Neither edge-case list (lines 193 and 259) includes zero-sum leadership, so the equivalence tests as specified would not catch it. Two additions close the gap:
- State the guard strategy for the leadership reduction (masked divide or `np.where` on the sum, same epsilon as 102).
- Add "all neighbors have zero leadership" and "stationary agent" (the `MomentumForce` epsilon from 102) to the edge-case list.

findings.title: Padded-array memory claim is wrong for the clustered case, and the "same interface" escape hatch does not exist
findings.description:
The design says memory only matters at "100K+" entities and that CSR gives "no benefit at n <= 10K". Padding is O(n_active × max_neighbors), and the slice's motivating scenario is clustering where k → n.

At 10K fully clustered agents:
- The index array alone is about 800 MB (10⁴ × 10⁴ × 8 bytes).
- Each gathered `(n, k, 2)` float64 temporary is about 1.6 GB, allocated per force, per tick.

One dense cluster also sets `max_neighbors` for every row. This sits inside the architecture's stated range ("tens of thousands of agents at full behavioral fidelity on a single CPU process") and runs against its notes on per-tick allocation and "no dynamic allocation" in the force path.

The mitigation offered, that CSR "would sit behind the same `NeighborData` interface", is not true as designed. Forces index `indices`, `mask` and `counts` directly, so a representation change rewrites every force. That is the consumer coupling the "Clean boundaries" goal rules out.

No new mechanism is needed in this slice. Correct the threshold, state the O(n × k_max) bound and the agent count this representation is valid for, and either drop the "same interface" claim or say plainly that a representation change is a force rewrite.

findings.title: Query-loop vectorization is attributed to slice 105, which does not own it
findings.description:
Lines 45, 101 and 184 defer the per-agent `query_radius` loop to 105 ("vectorizing the spatial query loop is 105's scope", "when slice 105 introduces a batch query"). The slice plan's 105 entry is only "replace the brute-force neighbor query with a spatial hash grid behind the existing query interface"; it contains no batch query and no interface change.

After 109 and 105 land as planned, the tick still has two O(n) Python passes (query, plus the new `build_neighbor_data`) and no slice owns removing them. Two consequences:
- The Overview's "constant Python overhead, regardless of agent count" holds for force functions only, not for the tick.
- The walkthrough's "ticks stay within 50 ms" result depends on loops this slice leaves in place.

Excluding the query loop is consistent with 109's plan entry. The fix is to state that the batch query is currently unowned, or add it to the 105 plan entry, and to scope the Overview claim to force computation.

findings.title: Slice 103's design and tasks are written against the signature this slice breaks
findings.description: 109 lists 103 under `interfaces` and says predator-prey forces will consume `NeighborData`. The existing 103 design sketches `FlightForce` and `PursuitForce` as per-agent loops over `neighbor_lists[list_idx]` with in-force self-exclusion. 103 is not started and the plan fixes no order between 103 and 109, so whichever lands second absorbs the change. A sentence saying so would prevent 103 from being implemented against a removed protocol.

findings.title: N-tick integration equivalence has no tolerance or horizon
findings.description: Per-force equivalence at `atol=1e-12` is sound. The integration test asserts that positions and velocities "match" after N ticks with no tolerance stated. A masked sum over padded rows adds in a different order than `np.mean` over a compact neighbor array, and flocking dynamics amplify last-bit differences. Specify a short horizon and a tolerance. Run-to-run determinism (the architecture goal) is unaffected.

findings.title: The 50 ms budget is verified only by a manual run
findings.description: The target is restated concretely (50 ms tick, 100 agents, `query_radius: 50.0`), but only in Value and the walkthrough. No Success Criteria item carries it, so every listed criterion can pass without the overrun being fixed. Promoting it to a Technical Requirement would close that.

findings.title: Two descriptive inaccuracies in the data-structure section
findings.description:
- **Padding dereference:** line 80 says `-1` padding is "never dereferenced", but the gather at line 111 does dereference it (it wraps to the last agent) and then zeroes the result. That is safe, but every reduction, including the separation distance filter, must apply the mask before use.
- **MomentumForce classification:** it is listed among the "five neighbor-dependent forces" (lines 35, 190) while line 125 says it uses no neighbor data.
